rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God begins proving the angels’ mistaken assumption by teaching Adam, demonstrating the superiority that had been announced to them.
rows.anchor: ولما أعلم سبحانه الملائكة أن الأمر على خلاف ما ظنوا شرع في إقامة الدليل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching is repeated instruction that makes knowledge settle, compensating for the teacher’s innate forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: والتعليم تكرار العلم ليثبت لما في جبلة المعلم من النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s name derives from adīm, the earth’s skin, from which his body was made; the earth-derived portion of him is reflected in his name.
rows.anchor: من الأدم من الأديم وهو جلدة الأرض التي منها جسمه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says “names” joins derivations from marking and elevation: as a word it marks, and as a share of a thing’s essence it is elevated.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع اسم وهو ما يجمع اشتقاقين من السمة والسمو

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes the spoken naming from a name as a portion of an object’s reality; the displayed objects are the latter, while the label corresponds to them.
rows.anchor: قاله الحرالي , وقال في كتاب له في أصول الفقه : الاسم يقال على لفظ التسمية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali explains that the displayed objects are shown from a side or aspect, which is the sense of ʿarḍ.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : أظهرهم عن جانب وهو العرض والناحية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Adam was taught the realities of all witnessed beings; angels saw their forms and the divine dominion but not the realities conveyed by their names, while Adam knew the relation between essences and their spoken labels.
rows.anchor: إحاطة علم آدم بما شهدوا صورة ولم يشهدوا حقيقة مدلول تسميتها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says Adam’s knowledge joined each created thing’s image with its divine command-word, completing what his heart apprehended through hearing and sight and preparing him to judge the created order.
rows.anchor: فيكمل علمه في قبله على سبيل سمعه وبصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displayed a form of intellectual and practical vicegerency through Adam’s naming, thereby exalting him before the angels.
rows.anchor: فأبدى الله عز وجل لهم بذلك وجه خلافة علمية وعملية في التسمية إعلاء له عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels immediately yielded to Adam’s superiority over all creation and learned that God raises whom He wills through His vicegerency of command and creation.
rows.anchor: فانقادوا للوقت بفضل آدم على جميع الخلق وبدا لهم علم أن الله يعلي من يشاء بما يشاء من خلافة أمره وخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural pronoun in “displayed them” encompasses the names as shares of the forms of all existing things; “these” points to them once the display is complete.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { ثم عرضهم } وأشار إليه ( هؤلاء ) عند كمال عرضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural pronoun applies because the displayed creatures include both rational and non-rational beings.
rows.anchor: وأجرى على الجميع ضمير ( هم ) لاشتمال تلك الكائنات على العاقلين وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi adds that every creature can speak when God makes it speak, as in the verse about bodily testimony on the Last Day.
rows.anchor: وبالتحقيق فكل خلق ناطق حين يستنطقه الحق

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي
rows.claim: Abu Hatim reports the grammarians’ derivation of “name” from elevation, then offers a wordplay: sīn suggests radiance and mīm the core, so a name illuminates an object’s essence; divine marks make names encompass knowledge of things.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي في كتاب الزينة : ويقال إن الاسم مأخوذ من السمو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God challenges the angels to report the names of the beings they had discerned, testing their earlier claim; the names and their referents have a wise correspondence established by the All-Knowing, All-Wise.
rows.anchor: بأسماء هؤلاء } أي الموجودات بتفرسكم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ “Glory be to You” absolves God of deficiency in knowledge or action and disclaims the implication that anyone else possesses independent knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي ننزهك تنزيها يجل عن الوصف عن أن ننسب إليك نقصا في علم أو صنع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali reads the angels’ admission as displaying their virtue, submission, and acquiescence, preparing for the ensuing mention of Iblis’s refusal.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي هذا المعنى إظهار لفضلهم وانقيادهم وإذعانهم توطئة لما يتصل به من إباء أبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ statement that they know only what God taught them establishes that there is no way to know anything except through His teaching.
rows.anchor: فهو دليل على أنه لا سبيل إلى علم شيء من الأشياء إلا بتعليم الله

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says this returns the beginning of the matter to its source; an unnamed transmitted maxim says one has not truly known unless one ends knowledge by recognizing ignorance apart from what God teaches.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : ردا لبدء الأمر لمن له البدء , ولذلك ورد في أثارة من علم : من لم يختم علمه بالجهل لم يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels reserve all knowledge and wisdom to God: He knows every object of knowledge and His wise acts cannot be corrupted, leaving no ground for objection.
rows.anchor: أي العالم بكل المعلومات { الحكيم } أي فلا يتطرق إلى صنعك فساد بوجه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali calls this an exclusive affirmation of divine knowledge and wisdom, a high form of surrender in which God adorns and gives life to hearts.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : توكيد وتخليص وإخلاص للعلم والحكمة لله وحده , وذلك من أرفع الإسلام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali compares knowledge and wisdom to light that gives life to hearts as water gives life to bodies, and defines wisdom as causal relation between two matters.
rows.anchor: فإن العلم والحكمة نور القلوب الذي تحيا به كما أن الماء رزق الأبدان الذي تحيا به

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines wisdom as a causal connection between two matters, with the prior one calling for and supporting the later one.
rows.anchor: والحكمة جعل تسبيب بين أمرين يبدو بينهما تقاض من السابق واستناد من اللاحق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says Adam is told to inform the angels so they gain insight that knowledge and felicity depend on what God teaches and grants.
rows.anchor: أي ليزدادوا بصيرة في أن العالم من علمته والسعيد من أسعدته

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Adam is described as informing rather than teaching: he already knew the names, while the angels received information and could not learn from him without Adam’s comprehensive created capacity.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : ولم يقل : علمهم , فكان آدم عليما بالأسماء وكانوا هم مخبرين بها لا معلميها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says every thing has two comprehensive names: one makes its existence perceptible and the other expresses its meaning toward its full reality; its many aspects yield distinct names and languages.
rows.anchor: والشيء اسمان جامعان : اسم بيصره من موجود الشيء واسم يذكره لإبداء معنى ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says names reflect the many aspects of things, producing diverse languages; Arabic is most eloquent and comprehensive, the language of the final revelation and of Paradise.
rows.anchor: ولكل اسم جامع عنده وجوه متعددة يحاذي كل وجه منها بتسمية تخصه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali calls Arabic the most eloquent and comprehensive language, the language of the final scripture and messengers and of Paradise, matching the ending to the beginning’s comprehensiveness.
rows.anchor: فأفصحها وأعربها الاسم الجامع وذلك الاسم هو العربي الذي به أنزل خاتم الكتب على خاتم المرسلين

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says divine lordship explains each rank according to the sign shown by its recipient; he links this to several verses about the Lord and His signs.
rows.anchor: فللربوبية بيان في كل رتبة بحسب ما أظهرته آية مربوبه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur’an’s address to the Prophet carries the greatest degree of understanding; forms of address vary with their hearers and divine attributes disclose different ranks of explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال في الباب الذي بعده : فخطاب الإقبال على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعظم إفهام في القرآن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali describes disclosure as unseen in signs to believers, direct vision for the fully certain, and comprehensive realization for the perfected knower; attention to these ranks opens further understanding.
rows.anchor: غيبا في متجلى الآيات للمؤمن , وعينا للكامل الموقن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says the Qur’an presents the beginning of creation in the order God brought it into being.
rows.anchor: وقد أوقع سبحانه ذكر ابتداء الخلق على ترتيب إيجاده له

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s chronology: soil on Saturday, mountains Sunday, trees Monday, harmful things Tuesday, light Wednesday, animals Thursday, and Adam after Friday afternoon, last among creation.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي فقال : ( خلق الله التربة يوم السبت

rows.speaker: المزي
rows.claim: Al-Mizzi cites al-Bukhari’s historical note that some authorities consider Abu Hurayra’s report from Kaʿb the more accurate attribution.
rows.anchor: وقال المزي في الأطراف قال البخاري في التاريخ : وقال بعضهم : أبو هريرة عن كعب وهو أصح .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi rejects as baseless the claim that earlier disobedient beings lived on earth and that the angels analogized Adam to them; the cited Muslim report makes Adam earth’s first inhabitant.
rows.anchor: وما يقال من أنه كان قبل آدم عليه السلام في الأرض خلق يعصون قاس عليهم الملائكة عليهم السلام حال آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says Adam’s name begins with the alphabet’s first letter and ends with its last, hinting that he was the first inhabitant while his descendants would be the last inhabitants before the Hour.
rows.anchor: والذي يلوح من اسمه في بدئه بالهمزة التي هي أول الحروف وختمه بالميم التي هي آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi quotes a Torah translation’s creation account: God made heaven, earth, light, waters, dry land, vegetation, celestial lights, sea and sky creatures, then land animals and humanity.
rows.anchor: ورأيت في ترجمة للتوراة وهو أولها : خلق الله ذات السماء وذات الأرض وكانت الظلمة فقال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted Torah account continues with humanity’s dominion, food, the completion of creation, and the claim that rain and cultivation awaited Adam’s creation.
rows.anchor: فخلق آدم بصورته ذكرا وأنثى وبارك عليهما وقال لهما : انميا وأكثرا وتسلطا على حيتان البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah passage says God formed Adam from earth, placed him in Eden, planted its trees, named its rivers, and prohibited eating from the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
rows.anchor: فجبل الله الرب آدم من تربة الأرض ونفخ في وجهه نسمة الحياة فصار آدم ذا نفس حية وغرس الله الرب فردوسا بعدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Torah account Adam names every living creature brought before him; God then makes a woman from his rib, and the pair become one flesh.
rows.anchor: وأقبل بها إلى آدم ليرى ما يسميها وكل نفس حية سماها آدم فذلك اسمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted Torah story recounts the serpent’s deception, the couple’s eating and shame, divine curses, expulsion from Eden, and a cherub guarding the tree of life; Adam lives 930 years.
rows.anchor: فأخرجه الله ربنا وأحاط من مشرق عدن ملكا من الكروبيين بيده حربة يطوف بها ليحرس طريق شجرة الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi explains “cherub” as a Hebrew word for a small person; cherubim are angels associated with people through revelation, named after the two figures between whom God’s speech was heard in the tabernacle.
rows.anchor: والكروب بوزن زبور بلغة العبرانيين الشخص الصغير , فكان الكروبيون الملائكة المنسوبين إلى مخالطة الناس بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi defends citing the Torah by arguing that an interlocutor should be answered from beliefs he accepts; he invokes Qur’anic commands to bring the Torah and its confirmation by the Qur’an, and recalls the Prophet’s use of Torah in an adultery case.
rows.anchor: قل فأتوا بالتوراة فاتلوها إن كنتم صادقين

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the earth will be served as a single loaf to the people of Paradise on the Resurrection Day; the Prophet smiles as a Jewish man confirms the report.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says the report of the Beast of the Earth is similar and groups such reports among matters confirmed by the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقريب من ذلك حديث الجساسة في أشباهه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet’s permission to narrate from the Children of Israel without blame.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet instructed Muslims not to affirm or deny People of the Book, but to say that they believe what was revealed to both communities.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : كان أهل الكتاب يقرؤون التوراة بالعبرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi reads these traditions as supporting the permissibility of transmitting such material, rather than prohibiting it; many Companions therefore took reports from People of the Book.
rows.anchor: فإن دلالة هذا على سنية ذكر مثل ذلك أقرب من الدلالة على غيرها

rows.speaker: الرافعي
rows.claim: Al-Rafiʿi and other Shafiʿi authorities are cited as saying that Torah and Gospel books may not be used because they were altered.
rows.anchor: قول الإمام أبي القاسم الرافعي في شرحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi limits that prohibition to material known to have been altered, since alteration is the stated rationale and al-Shafiʿi’s own texts allow other material to be used.
rows.anchor: هذا مخصوص بما علم تبديله , بدليل أن كل من قال ذلك علل بالتبديل

rows.speaker: المزني
rows.claim: Al-Muzani says non-disliked medical or other useful books taken from unbelievers may be sold, while books containing shirk are destroyed and their containers retained for use.
rows.anchor: قال المزني في مختصره في باب جامع السير : وما كان من كتبهم أي الكفار فيه طب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says captured books should be translated; useful material without objection may be sold, while books of shirk are split and their materials retained, with no destruction before their contents are examined.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي : وما وجد من كتبهم فهو مغنم كله , وينبغي للإمام أن يدعو من يترجمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi reads al-Shafiʿi’s phrase “book of shirk” as suggesting the whole book is shirk, whereas al-Muzani’s wording allows that only some chapters contain it.
rows.anchor: فقوله في الأم : كتاب شرك , مفهم لأنه كله شرك

rows.speaker: النواوي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi records a preferred Shafiʿi position that touching Torah or Gospel while in minor ritual impurity has the same rule as touching a Qur’anic passage whose recitation was abrogated.
rows.anchor: محرر المذهب الشيخ محيي الدين النواوي رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi infers from calling this the preferred of two positions that the alternative view forbidding an impure person to touch or carry such books is also substantial.
rows.anchor: حكم ما نسخت تلاوته من القرآن في أصح الوجهين

rows.speaker: المتولي
rows.claim: Al-Mutawalli says touching a passage thought to be unaltered is disliked; Biqaʿi treats the dislike as respect, implying that preservation and reading are permitted.
rows.anchor: أن المتولي قال : فإن ظن أن فيها شيئا غير مبدل كره مسه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s statement that books without objection may be sold supports the permissibility of retaining and using them.
rows.anchor: وأصرح من ذلك كله قول الشافعي رحمه الله : إن ما لا مكروه فيه يباع

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says a person in major ritual impurity may utter words coinciding with Qur’anic wording, abrogated verses, Torah or Gospel, remembrance of God, or blessings on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قول البغوي في تهذيبه في آخر باب الوضوء

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿAʾisha reports that the Prophet remembered God in every state, which al-Baghawi uses as evidence for the permissibility of such utterances.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر الله على كل أحيانه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi argues that whatever may be read by a person in major impurity without necessity may be read by one in minor impurity, but not vice versa; this does not make every passage lawful, and the relevant words count as remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا يتخيل أنه يجوز للجنب ما لا يجوز للمحدث

rows.speaker: القاضي الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Qadi al-Husayn says one may clean oneself with the Torah and Gospel, based on the position that all of both books have been altered.
rows.anchor: قول القاضي الحسين : إنه يجوز الاستنجاء بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi calls that position weak or restricts it to altered text, since no Muslim would use the Ten Commandments as a means of cleaning himself.
rows.anchor: وهو ضعيف أو محمول على المبدل منهما , لأنه لا يخفى على أحد

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar’s conclusion permits learned scholars grounded in religious sciences to consult these books and extract benefits for the guided, while others may not; Biqaʿi endorses the distinction.
rows.anchor: شيخنا حافظ عصره أبو الفضل بن حجر في آخر شرحه للبخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says he composed a separate work on the ruling of transmitting from ancient scriptures, titled “Al-Aqwal al-Qawima fi Hukm al-Naql min al-Kutub al-Qadima.”
rows.anchor: ثم صنفت في ذلك تصنيفا حسنا سميته ( الأقوال القويمة في حكم النقل من الكتب القديمة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi distinguishes three Torah versions—the Septuagint, the Rabbinic and Karaite text, and the Samaritan text—which differ in wording but are close in meaning; he recounts the Septuagint’s translation by 72 Jewish scholars.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن التوراة ثلاث نسخ مختلفة اللفظ متقاربة المعنى إلا يسيرا : إحداها تسمى توراة السبعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says the Septuagint was translated into Syriac and Arabic and was held by Christians; he notes that al-Samarqandi, al-Taftazani, and Qadi ʿIyad cited Torah passages on theology.
rows.anchor: وهذه النسخة ترجمت بعد بالسرياني ثم بالعربي وهي في أيدي النصارى ؛ والنسخة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi describes his own old Torah copy as probably Jewish, with damaged lines restored from a Septuagint copy and its wording compared against Saʿadia al-Fayyumi’s translation with a Jewish reader; he judges his copy closer to Hebrew and its translator more skilled in Arabic.
rows.anchor: ثم اعلم أن أكثر ما ذكرته في كتابي هذا من نسخة وقعت لي لم أدر اسم مترجمها
